## Amendment A6 (owner, 2026-11-26) — read before the sections below

Amendment A6 — the five finders run when reproduction is unavailable (owner decision, 2026-11-26): A1's
preflight sent a branch with no ledger entry to the single reviewer when `review-repro.sh 'true'` refused, and in the
eval sandbox it always refuses (A5), so no replay would run the exhaustive round. Now the exhaustive round runs
whenever the route is light or full, whatever the preflight says: when review-repro.sh refuses (exit 2), the round
runs with reproduction unavailable — the verifier marks every blocker UNREPRODUCED with the refusal as its reason, and
under decision 3 an UNREPRODUCED blocker still blocks. A1's single-reviewer fallback is removed; on a ledger item the
review is no longer INCOMPLETE for this reason (it is the same round, without reproduction); the preflight's refusal
is still reported in the summary with its cause and fix line. Task T023a implements this.

## Amendment A5 (owner, 2026-11-24) — read before the sections below

Amendment A5 — evals grade findings, not reproduction (owner decision, 2026-11-24, after the third probe 2): the
eval sandbox has no writable temp folder and no writable folder under the cache, so review-repro.sh cannot make a
scratch copy there and no recipe runs (evals/README.md, "Probes"). Reproduction in a real verify worker is proven by
probe 1 and is measured by real verify runs, not by the evals. So, in the replay evals only: a corpus defect counts as
found when a BLOCKING finding names it, whether REPRODUCED or UNREPRODUCED (under decision 3 an UNREPRODUCED blocker
still blocks, so the verdict REQUEST_CHANGES is still graded); the `tool_used Bash input_match review-repro.sh`
grader is dropped from the cases (the verifier may still try a recipe); every case's llm criteria say so. FR-016 and
FR-019 change accordingly; review-repro.sh, its refusals and amendments A3/A4 stay as built. T016 is done with probe 2
recorded as "reproduction unavailable in the eval sandbox"; the build continues at T017 (task T016c applies A5 to the
two existing cases first). No more probe rounds.

## Amendment A4 (owner, 2026-11-24) — read before the sections below

Amendment A4 — reproduction in the eval sandbox (owner decision, 2026-11-24, after the second probe 2): the eval
sandbox gives the model a fresh $HOME with no ~/.cache/hefesto and a read-only temp folder, so review-repro.sh refused
(exit 2) before running the recipe. A real verify worker has both (probe 1). Wanted: each replay case's scaffold
(tests/fixtures/review-replay.sh, run as the person with --scaffold) creates "$HOME/.cache/hefesto" for the eval home;
review-repro.sh makes its scratch copy under its cache folder when the temp folder is not writable, and still refuses
loudly when neither is; the 18 replay cases stay as planned. Task T016b implements this.

## Amendment A3 (owner, 2026-11-23) — read before the sections below

Amendment A3 — the recipe channel (owner decision, 2026-11-23, after eval probe 2): in the eval sandbox the temp
folder is read-only, so a heredoc cannot be created and review-repro.sh never starts (evals/README.md, "Probes"). The
recipe therefore reaches review-repro.sh as ONE single-quoted argument: `<abs hooks>/review-repro.sh '<recipe>'`.
Heredoc/stdin input stays supported where it works (the verify worker, probe 1). This SUPERSEDES, for the recipe only:
plan.md:45 ("There is no argument-form fallback"), FR-006's "recipe on stdin", FR-022's "a quoted heredoc" for
review-repro.sh, spec.md:138-144 and Sketch 6. In a lane, lane-guard.sh admits only the exact two-word head: the
plugin's absolute review-repro.sh path plus one single-quoted string with no `'` inside, with the same near-miss
denials as the heredoc exception, each with a mutation test. code-review-check's report keeps its heredoc (FR-011
unchanged) unless the d22-3 replay shows it failing in the eval sandbox. Task T016a implements this.

## Truth map — the verify permission surface

| Fact | Source |
|------|--------|
| The headless verify worker's allow list: `Read`, `Glob`, `Grep`, `Skill`, `Agent`, `Bash(git diff*)`, `Bash(git log*)` (or the project's `orchestrate.allowed_tools.verify`), always plus `Bash(<hooks>/*)` | `session-launch.sh:209-215`; `.claude/project-status.json` |
| Prompts are off — anything outside the list is denied, never asked | `session-launch.sh:662` |
| `Edit` and `Write` are disallowed outright in verify | `session-launch.sh:675` |
| The worker runs in the OS sandbox: writes only to the worktree and the worker cache; `$TMPDIR` is sandbox-writable; the main repository's `.git` is not writable from a headless worker | `session-launch.sh:303-307` |
| A lane verify is told to call every helper as one plain command | `session-launch.sh:635` |
| In a lane, `lane-guard.sh` matches an excluded command's word (e.g. `gh`) anywhere in the command text, heredoc bodies included, and then admits only one plain word list starting with that word, or a heredoc for `ledger.sh answer|revise|direct` | `lane-guard.sh:66-114` |
| Later rules still read the hit: an excluded word beside `lane-build`/`lane-cache` is denied (`:88-90`); a non-`gh`, non-hefesto excluded word is denied unless granted (`:229-234`); a `gh` hit not matching `GH_READ` is denied in a `--lanes` project (`:243-246`) | `lane-guard.sh:88-90, 222-246` |
| Setup's lane allow list holds `speckit-helper.sh:*` and other helpers, not a new helper; a `--strict` project (`autoAllowBashIfSandboxed` false) asks for anything not listed | `hefesto-setup.sh:194-196` |
| `lane-build.sh` runs a command only with `HEFESTO_LANE_CACHE` set (lanes), never headless | `hooks/lane-build.sh:27-29` |
| `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is substituted in a command's body text, not set in the Bash env; subagents inherit the parent's permissions | constitution, Architecture Constraints |

**Derived:** a verifier cannot run `bash -c '<recipe>'`, write a fixture, or `mkdir` a scratch folder. The channel is a
plugin helper (`Bash(<hooks>/*)`), called as one plain command with a quoted heredoc. In a lane that heredoc is denied
when its body names `gh` (a report or recipe about `pr-watch.sh` will) — so `lane-guard.sh` gets a narrow exception
(FR-022): the head is exactly `<abs path>/hooks/speckit-helper.sh code-review-check` or `<abs path>/hooks/review-repro.sh`
(plain words, `plain_words`), the delimiter is quoted (`<<'WORD'`), the last line is the delimiter **and the only
line equal to it** (bash ends a heredoc at the first such line; anything after an early one would run as commands no
rule read — round 4, change 1), and `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` is not set (Sketch 6). Those helpers are not excluded commands, so the call runs inside the sandbox
and the excluded word is data (the reasoning already in `lane-guard.sh:72-75`). **The exception is its own path that
ends the guard:** `review_heredoc_ok` is decided right after the excluded-word scan (after `:81`, before `:88`, with
`words()` from `:104` and the `DDS` line from `:86` moved above it so the function can use them) and,
when it holds, the hook `exit 0`s with no decision — the permission rules then allow it (`speckit-helper.sh:*`, and
the new `review-repro.sh:*` rule) — so `:88-90`, `:109`, `:229-234` and `:243-246` never read the body. It is not a
third arm of `heredoc_ok`, which requires `starts_bare` and `*/ledger.sh` (`:99-100`). A path that merely ends in
`/hooks/review-repro.sh` but is not the plugin's passes this hook and is still unmatched by any allow rule, so it is
denied or asked as today. There is no argument-form fallback: the same regex denies it.

**Setup (round 3, change 2):** `hefesto-setup.sh:196` gains `"Bash($h/review-repro.sh:*)"`, so a `--strict` lane runs
recipes without a dialog; `tests/smoke-github-board.sh`'s check over that list is updated with it.

**The helper enforces the sandbox (round 3, change 2):** like `lane-build.sh:31-34`, `review-repro.sh` first checks
that `$(hef_cache)` exists — missing → exit 2, "review-repro.sh: $(hef_cache) is missing, so the sandbox cannot be
probed — run hefesto-setup.sh" (a missing folder is never read as "sandboxed", `lane-build.sh:31`; fixture +
mutation). Every launched worker has it (the launcher makes `$(hef_cache)/worker-cache/…` there, `session-launch.sh:303`).
Then it tries a write to `$(hef_cache)/.repro-probe.<pid>` (`hef_cache` from `lane-lib.sh`; outside every sandbox's
`allowWrite` — the worker's is `$(hef_cache)/worker-cache/<repo>`, a lane's `$(hef_cache)/lane-cache/<key>`). The write
succeeding means the call is not sandboxed: the file is removed and the helper exits 2, "review-repro.sh: not running inside the OS
sandbox — recipes run sandboxed only". The smoke suite (unsandboxed) runs the helper with `HOME` pointing at a temp
home whose `.cache/hefesto` it made read-only (`chmod 555`) — `hef_cache` is `$HOME/.cache/hefesto`
(`lane-lib.sh:10`), so this is the knob the probe already reads, no new seam; the 19s fixture asserts the
refusal with a writable cache, and a mutation that drops the probe makes it go red. Like `lane-build.sh`, a caller who
controls the environment and runs unsandboxed can defeat it; it stops the careless path (a retry with the sandbox
off), and the lane guard additionally refuses `dangerouslyDisableSandbox` on these heredocs.

## Data Model

No data model changes. The report is text with a fixed shape (Implementation 1); the ledger, its schema and the
launcher's schema are unchanged. `review-route` only reads the ledger.

## API Contracts

**`speckit-helper.sh code-review-check`** — stdin: the merged report **without** a verdict or `BLOCKING` line.
- Exit 0, stdout: `## Verdict: APPROVE|REQUEST_CHANGES` then the `BLOCKING` line — decided by the D6 rule from the
  statuses (a `REPRODUCED` or `UNREPRODUCED` `[BLOCKING]` finding → `REQUEST_CHANGES`). The command appends both.
- Exit 1, stdout: `## Verdict: INCOMPLETE` then the `BLOCKING` line of every blocker the report does establish (it may
  be `BLOCKING 0:`); stderr: one line per violation, `code-review-check: [shape|content] <rule>: <offending text>`.
  The stdout cannot be mistaken for a pass — it says `INCOMPLETE` (constitution 5).
- Exit 2: empty stdin.
- Violations: a lens section missing or empty; a bare `none`; a `Finders:` line without five entries or with one
  `silent`; a `[BLOCKING]` finding without a status; a finding line or recipe block malformed; the report carrying a
  `## Verdict` or `BLOCKING` line of its own. `[shape]` = format only; `[content]` = something missing.

**Invocation** — one plain command starting with the helper's absolute path (the command's body text has it
substituted), a quoted heredoc, no pipe, no `Write`:
```
<abs hooks>/speckit-helper.sh code-review-check <<'HEF_CRC_REPORT_END'
<the merged report>
HEF_CRC_REPORT_END
```

**`speckit-helper.sh review-route [--inline]`** — stdout one line `exhaustive <route> <source>` or
`single <route> <source>`, source `ledger:<ID>` | `spec:<dir>` | `no-spec` | `inline`; an `exhaustive` line always
ends with ` spec:<abs dir>` (round 5, change 3) — on the ledger path the entry's folder from `spec_dir_abs`
(`spec-root-lib.sh:111`, already sourced by the helper; the launcher resolves it the same way,
`session-launch.sh:242`), and a `light`/`full` entry whose folder is empty or holds no readable `spec.md` exits 1
naming the entry and the path. The command writes that folder into every finder and verifier brief ("the spec is in
<dir>: read spec.md and plan.md there"), since a `worktree-<ID>` branch does not resolve it (`hef.review.md:22-25`). Branch: `$BRANCH`, else the
`ref: refs/heads/<name>` line of `.git/HEAD` (a linked worktree's `.git` file is followed to its `gitdir`), else exit
1 `review-route: cannot read the branch (git denied and no readable .git/HEAD)`; a detached HEAD → exit 1. Item
(round 3, change 3): **only** for a branch `worktree-<ID>` is `ledger.sh dir` asked — its failure there exits 1
naming the ledger error (never a fall-through to the spec folder); `<dir>/<ID>.json` exists → the entry's
`.route // "fix"`; the file exists but `ledger.sh show <ID>` fails or the JSON does not parse → exit 1 naming the
entry and the error; no such file → the spec folder. Any other branch (a person's, an eval scaffold's — where git is
denied and `ledger.sh dir` would die, `ledger.sh:253-256`) never touches the ledger. Spec folder: `review-route` is
added to the spec-root list (`speckit-helper.sh:53-55`, #172), so it runs from the spec root and an app folder's spec
resolves; `.specify/specs/<branch minus feature/>/spec.md` there → `exhaustive full spec:<abs dir>` — the
absolute path, `$(pwd -P)/.specify/specs/<branch>` from the spec root (amendment A3), like the ledger path — else
`single fix no-spec`. The app-folder fixture asserts the absolute path.

**`hooks/review-repro.sh`** — stdin: the recipe, saved to `<scratch>/.hef-recipe.sh` before anything runs. Stdout:
`exit: <n>` then the output, capped at 60 lines **and** 8 KiB (`… +<k> lines / <b> bytes cut`). Exit 0 after a run,
whatever the recipe's status (the status is data); 2 = refused (not inside the OS sandbox, empty recipe, no scratch
folder, no worktree); 3 = the worktree changed during the run (each path on stderr, `created|modified|deleted
<path>`).
- **The copy (round 2, changes 2 and 10):** the files `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` lists
  (tracked plus unignored — never `.git`, never `node_modules`/`target` when ignored); when git cannot run, `find`
  with `.git` (file or directory) pruned. Then, when git runs, `git init -q` + a commit with a fixed identity in the
  scratch copy, so a recipe's `git config`/`git commit`/refs act on the scratch repository. Environment:
  `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` unset. The recipe is never told where the real worktree is (round 3,
  change 6): everything it needs is in the copy, cwd-relative.
- **The run:** `bash .hef-recipe.sh </dev/null` with the scratch copy as cwd; `timeout 60` when present (stock macOS:
  untimed, said on stderr). The verifier brief calls the helper with the Bash tool's `timeout: 300000`, so copy +
  init + recipe + both listings finish well inside the tool's limit and the after-listing always runs (round 4,
  change 3).
- **Cleanup:** `trap 'rm -rf "$scratch"' EXIT` set right after `mktemp -d`, so the copy goes on every exit path —
  success, exit 3, a timed-out recipe, a refusal after the folder was made (fixture: no `hef-repro.*` left in the test
  `TMPDIR` after each of those).
- **The guard (change 9; primitive, round 4 change 3):** before the run, one line per tracked + unignored worktree
  file, `cksum <path>` (POSIX: checksum, size, path — catches a same-size rewrite within one timestamp tick), sorted,
  into the scratch folder; after it, the same listing; `diff` (POSIX) of the two → each `<`/`>` line becomes
  `created|modified|deleted <path>` on stderr and exit 3. The file list is `git ls-files -z --cached --others
  --exclude-standard` when git runs, else `find` with `.git` pruned — so a gitignored path is in neither listing and a
  build output does not trip it. Cost: two checksum passes over the tree per recipe (Known limits). The verifier records the candidate as
  `UNREPRODUCED — the recipe wrote into the worktree: <paths>`, and the command lists the paths under Open questions.
  Parallel verifiers only write scratch copies, so they cannot trip each other.

## Implementation Approach

1. **The report contract** (changes 7 and 13). In order: `Finders:` line — five entries
   `<lens>@<tier asked for> ok|silent: <why>`; four `## Lens: <name>` sections, each holding findings or one
   `none — checked: …` line; `## Open questions`. A finding is one line, then its recipe as an indented fenced block:
   ```
   - [F3] [BLOCKING] hooks/forge-lib.sh:33 — internal-host deny list is case-sensitive — raised by: input-and-security, cross-tier — REPRODUCED → exit: 0 / "allowed"
       ```recipe F3
       . hooks/forge-lib.sh; fg_host_denied metadata.google.INTERNAL && echo denied || echo allowed   # cwd = the scratch copy
       ```
   ```
   The recipe block is the stdin the verifier passes to `review-repro.sh`, between `<<'HEF_REPRO_RECIPE_END'` and
   `HEF_REPRO_RECIPE_END`. Both delimiters are long and distinct, so a recipe inside a report inside the check's
   heredoc is literal text. The verdict and the `BLOCKING` line are the helper's output, never written by an agent.
2. **Absolute paths in every brief.** The command's body text has `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` substituted; it writes the
   resolved `<abs hooks>/review-repro.sh` into each finder and verifier brief (subagents get no substitution).
3. **Route first (D11, FR-021).** `review-route` (with `--inline` when given). `single` → today's code-mode section,
   brief and relay **unchanged, byte for byte**, under a `### Single reviewer` heading. Exit ≠ 0 → `INCOMPLETE` with
   the helper's message (never a silent fall-back to one reviewer — US7).
3a. **Preflight (amendment A1).** After an `exhaustive` answer, one trivial call
   `<abs hooks>/review-repro.sh <<'HEF_REPRO_RECIPE_END'` / `true` / `HEF_REPRO_RECIPE_END`. Exit 0 → the round. Exit 2
   (not inside the sandbox, or `$(hef_cache)` missing — a refusal for the whole environment): on a route whose source
   is not `ledger:<ID>` (a person's own branch) → the single reviewer, the report opening with one line
   `exhaustive round unavailable: <helper's message> — fix: <run inside the sandbox / run hefesto-setup.sh>`; on a
   `ledger:<ID>` route → `INCOMPLETE` naming the cause, never a fall-back. A structural check in part 19 asserts the
   preflight and both outcomes are in `commands/hef.review.md`; `docs/commands.md` gains one line on it.
4. **The round.** Five `code-reviewer` spawns in one message, foreground (four `lens: <name>` at the pinned tier, the
   fifth all lenses with `model: opus`). Merge: same `file:line` + same failure → one candidate, every lens kept, and
   **`BLOCKING` if any lens said so** (change 6). Verifier `code-reviewer`(s) get the **blocking** candidates only, ≤ 8
   each, one message; a `SUGGESTION` is listed with `not verified — never blocks` and needs no status (round 5, change
   4 — matches `crc_statuses_ok`, which checks `[BLOCKING]` lines only; a fixture shows a status-less suggestion
   passes and a status-less blocker does not).
5. **Severity (change 6).** The Finder role carries the blocking criterion: `BLOCKING` only for a defect that breaks
   correctness, security or a stated requirement; everything else `SUGGESTION`. The verifier marks `REFUTED` a
   blocking candidate whose recipe runs but shows no defect of that class (quoting why), so a reproduced nit does not
   block.
6. **One retry before `INCOMPLETE`** (FR-009/FR-011). A silent finder or verifier is re-spawned once with the same
   brief, in the same turn. A check exit 1 whose violations are all `[shape]` → re-write the report once from the same
   agent outputs and re-check.
7. **Where the builder reads each blocker (change 8).** Evidence (≤ 500, `session-launch.sh:564`) leads with the
   `BLOCKING` line — also on `INCOMPLETE`, where the reason follows it (`… ; INCOMPLETE: <first violation>`), cut at
   500. Each entry is `<file:line> (<lens>) <defect in ≤ 8 words>`, `unreproduced` appended where it applies. The run
   summary (≤ 2000, shared by every gate) carries `Review recipes:` — `F<n>: <recipe's first line, ≤ 150 chars>` per
   blocker, cut with `… +<k> more`; the transcript holds the rest.
8. **Verify-run fit:** `INCOMPLETE` is reported as gate `review` `FAIL`. No launcher edit.
9. **`--second-opinion` in code mode.** An exhaustive round's prompt file carries the cross-tier finder's brief (all
   four lenses, recipe per candidate) then the spec and the capped diff; the single path sends today's brief.
10. **Rules scoped to roles.** In `agents/code-reviewer.md`, Critical Rule 0, Rule 1 and the Verdict Criteria keep
    today's text and gain one opening clause, "Outside the finder and verifier roles"; the two role sections carry
    their own rules (exhaustive; precision is the verifier's; no verdict — the helper decides). Plan mode's brief, the
    single-reviewer brief and `/hefesto:hef.verify`'s Stage-1-only spawn are not edited.

## Code Sketches (Mental Alignment)

### Sketch 1: code mode orchestration
**File:** `commands/hef.review.md` (modify at `:116-138`)

```markdown
## Code mode
Run with the Bash tool: `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/speckit-helper.sh review-route [--inline]`
`single …` → "### Single reviewer" (today's section, unchanged). Exit ≠ 0 → INCOMPLETE (helper message).
`exhaustive …` → preflight `review-repro.sh` with `true`; exit 2 → no-ledger source: single reviewer + cause line;
ledger source: INCOMPLETE (cause).
### Exhaustive round — five finders by lens, a verifier, one verdict
1. ONE message, foreground: code-reviewer ×5 — four `lens: <name>` (pinned tier), one cross-tier `model: opus`;
   each brief names `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/review-repro.sh` (substituted here, absolute).
2. Silent one → re-spawn once. Merge (BLOCKING wins). Number F1…Fn.
3. Verifier(s), ≤ 8 each, one message: each recipe via `<abs>/review-repro.sh <<'HEF_REPRO_RECIPE_END'`.
4. Write the report (no verdict); run the check heredoc; [shape]-only → one re-format; append its stdout.
5. Relay; in a verify run: INCOMPLETE → review FAIL, evidence leads with BLOCKING, summary gets `Review recipes:`.
```

### Sketch 2: lenses and roles in the agent
**File:** `agents/code-reviewer.md` (new sections after `:82`; clauses on Rules 0/1 `:124-130`, Verdict Criteria `:138`)

```markdown
## Lenses (exhaustive code review)
- **input-and-security** — untrusted input, quoting into shells/git, parsing external output, bypass spellings, secrets
- **state-and-lifecycle** — writes before a failure/refusal, reruns, removal symmetry, ordering/races, stale records
- **spec-deviation** — each FR/plan decision: missing, partial, regressed, or success reported while not done
- **test-integrity** — tests that cannot fail, never run, assert on fakeable data, weakened; cite vs exercise
## Finder role — every candidate: file:line + a recipe block; BLOCKING only for correctness/security/a stated
   requirement; nothing → `none — checked: <what>`; no verdict
## Verifier role — each recipe via review-repro.sh; one status each; REFUTED when it runs but shows no defect of its
   class; never edit; never add findings; no verdict
0. Outside the finder and verifier roles: evidence over assertion, and scope over volume. … (today's text)
```

### Sketch 3: the check and the route
**File:** `hooks/code-review-lib.sh` (new), dispatched beside `plan-review-round` (`speckit-helper.sh:508`)

```bash
crc_check() {   # stdin: report → stdout verdict + BLOCKING line; 0 decided, 1 INCOMPLETE (violations on stderr), 2 empty
  local r; r="$(cat)"; [ -n "$r" ] || { echo "code-review-check: empty report — nothing to check" >&2; return 2; }
  local bad=0 lens
  for lens in input-and-security state-and-lifecycle spec-deviation test-integrity; do crc_lens_ok "$r" "$lens" || bad=1; done
  crc_finders_ok "$r" || bad=1; crc_statuses_ok "$r" || bad=1; crc_no_verdict "$r" || bad=1
  if [ "$bad" = 1 ]; then echo "## Verdict: INCOMPLETE"; else crc_verdict "$r"; fi   # D6 rule, UNREPRODUCED blocks
  crc_blocking_line "$r"                                                            # ≤ 500, "… +k more"
  return "$bad"
}
crc_route() {   # → "exhaustive|single <route> <source>"; 1 on no branch, detached, unreadable entry
  [ "${1:-}" = --inline ] && { echo "single - inline"; return 0; }
  local br="$BRANCH" id d; [ -n "$br" ] || br="$(crc_head_branch)" || return 1   # .git/HEAD (file → gitdir; strips feature/) or die
  id="${br#worktree-}"
  if [ "$id" != "$br" ]; then                       # only a worktree-<ID> branch asks the ledger
    d="$("$(dirname "$SELF")/ledger.sh" dir)" || { echo "review-route: ledger dir failed for $id" >&2; return 1; }
    [ -f "$d/$id.json" ] && { crc_route_from_entry "$id"; return; }   # show + jq, or exit 1 naming it
  fi
  # cwd is the spec root here (review-route is in the list at speckit-helper.sh:53-55)
  if [ -f ".specify/specs/$br/spec.md" ]; then echo "exhaustive full spec:$(pwd -P)/.specify/specs/$br"   # absolute (A3); $br has no feature/
  else echo "single fix no-spec"; fi
}
```

**Why this shape:** each rule is one function, so each mutation removes exactly one rule; the verdict is computed,
so the "verdict contradicts the statuses" class cannot occur (round 2, change 13).

### Sketch 4: replay scaffold and a case
**File:** `tests/fixtures/review-replay.sh` (new), `evals/review-replay-d22-3/{case.yaml,scaffold.sh}` (new)

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# review-replay.sh <base-sha> <head-sha> <spec> — a two-commit repo in the CWD: main = base, feature/<spec> = head
set -euo pipefail
R="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"; base=$1 head=$2 spec=$3
for c in "$base" "$head"; do git -C "$R" cat-file -e "$c^{commit}" 2>/dev/null \
  || { echo "review-replay: commit $c is not in $R — a shallow clone? fetch main's full history" >&2; exit 1; }; done
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=hefesto-eval GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL=eval@example.invalid \
       GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=hefesto-eval GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=eval@example.invalid
git init -q -b main . && git -C "$R" archive "$base" | tar -x && git add -A && git commit -qm base
git checkout -qb "feature/$spec" && git ls-files -z | xargs -0 rm -f
git -C "$R" archive "$head" | tar -x && git add -A && git commit -qm "change under review"
git diff main...HEAD > .git/hef-review.diff   # the eval sandbox denies git to the model (evals/README.md:27)
```
```yaml
schema_version: "1.1"
name: review-replay-d22-3
plugins: ["../.."]
context: { scaffold_script: scaffold.sh }
execution:
  prompt: "/hefesto:hef.review code — git may be unavailable here: the change under review (base main) is .git/hef-review.diff"
  max_turns: 80
  timeout_seconds: 2400
  allowed_tools: [Agent, Bash, Read, Glob, Grep, Skill]   # amendment A2: every replay and probe case carries it
graders:
  - { name: five-finders-and-a-verifier, type: tool_used, tool: Agent, min: 6 }
  - { name: verifier-ran-a-recipe, type: tool_used, tool: Bash, input_match: "review-repro\\.sh", min: 1 }
  - name: finds-d22-3
    type: llm
    criteria: "PASS only if the verdict is REQUEST_CHANGES and a BLOCKING finding marked REPRODUCED says hooks/forge-lib.sh's internal-host deny list is case-sensitive …"
```
**Whole tree, deliberately** (round 2, change 11): `git archive` takes the whole tree, `.claude/` and `CLAUDE.md`
included — the original reviews ran under that project config, so the replay keeps it in both arms. Each case's
`scaffold.sh` is `exec "$(dirname "$0")/../../tests/fixtures/review-replay.sh" <full base> <full head> <spec>` with
full 40-char SHAs. **Runs:** one per arm (the CLI default). **Operator grant:** `--allow-tools Bash`. **The
with-without arm applies:** the without arm has no `/hefesto:hef.review` and is expected to fail — the baseline,
recorded as such; the cost table records the with arm. The `review-repro.sh` grader stays on all 15 per-defect cases
(round 3, change 5): in the six finding-alone cases the verifier still runs a recipe — one that fails for want of git
or host state yields `UNREPRODUCED`, and the call happened — so FR-016 and FR-019 hold as written.

**Control cases (round 3, change 4):** `review-control-hef-22|25|31` scaffold the item's diff base and its merged
head (the item branch's last commit, the merge commit's second parent, resolved to a full SHA at build time). Graders:
`tool_used Agent min 6` (the round ran) and an `llm` grader that PASSes when the report ends with a verdict and a
`BLOCKING <n>:` line — measurement, not a claim; the results table records the verdict and `<n>` (blockers on a head
the old review passed, so each is either a defect the old review missed or a false block, read by the person).

**Known limits of `review-repro.sh`, recorded in `docs/agents.md`:** each recipe copies every tracked and unignored
file and checksums the worktree twice — linear in the tree's size, unbounded on a large adopting repository (no cap
in this item; the replay's wall-time column shows the cost here); a lane body may not name the
`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=` assignment (Sketch 6).

**Known limits, recorded in `evals/README.md`:** (1) the answer key is readable in the with arm — the plugin root at
HEAD holds the fixed hooks, this spec's corpus table, the CHANGELOG and the case rubrics; the replay measures the
round, not a blind reviewer, and a transcript that reads them is a failed run to discard. (2) An `llm` grader can
only read the report; the `review-repro.sh` grader is the tool-level proof that something ran (constitution 3), if the
probe shows `tool_used` sees a subagent's calls — otherwise that grader is recorded as main-session-only.

### Sketch 6: the lane-guard exception — its own path, ending the guard (round 4, changes 1 and 2)
**File:** `hooks/lane-guard.sh` (new function and one call after the excluded-word scan `:81` and before `:88`, with
`words()` and the `DDS` line moved above it)

```bash
# FR-022 (HEF-58): the review round's two helpers take a report or a recipe as a quoted heredoc, and that text names
# gh and other excluded words as data. The helpers are not excluded, so the call runs inside the sandbox. Admitted
# only in this exact shape; then nothing below reads the body. Placed AFTER the CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID deny (:64),
# which stays in force for these bodies too.
review_heredoc_ok() {
  local first last word head n=0 line
  [ "$DDS" = true ] && return 1                                        # never with the sandbox off
  first="${CMD%%$'\n'*}"; last="${CMD##*$'\n'}"; [ "$first" != "$CMD" ] || return 1
  [[ "$first" =~ \<\<\'([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]{3,40})\'[[:space:]]*$ ]] || return 1
  word="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"; [ "$last" = "$word" ] || return 1
  while IFS= read -r line; do [ "$line" = "$word" ] && n=$((n + 1)); done <<<"$CMD"
  [ "$n" = 1 ] || return 1                                             # an earlier delimiter ends the heredoc early
  head="${first%<<*}"; plain_words "$head" || return 1
  local -a w=(); while IFS= read -r line; do w+=("$line"); done < <(words "$head")   # the exact word list
  [[ "${w[0]:-}" == /* ]] || return 1                                  # an absolute path first: no word, no X=… before it
  case "${#w[@]}:${w[0]}" in                                           # the count is part of the match — no `*` over spaces
    1:*/hooks/review-repro.sh) return 0 ;;
    2:*/hooks/speckit-helper.sh) [ "${w[1]}" = code-review-check ] && return 0 ;;
  esac; return 1
}
```
**Placement (round 5, change 2):** the call must come before the lane-build/lane-cache deny (`:88-90`) and the
excluded-command denies (`:106-114`, `:229-246`), but `words()` is defined only at `:104` and `DDS` at `:86`. So both
definitions move up, unchanged, to just after the excluded-word scan (`:81`), followed by the function and its call
(`plain_words` comes from `lane-lib.sh`, already sourced):
```bash
words() { … }                       # moved up from :104, unchanged
DDS="$(jq -r '.tool_input.dangerouslyDisableSandbox // false' <<<"$IN")"   # moved up from :86, unchanged
review_heredoc_ok && exit 0         # no decision: the permission rules (speckit-helper.sh:*, review-repro.sh:*) decide
```
A `*/hooks/review-repro.sh` path that is not the plugin's still passes this hook only to meet the permission rules,
which allow the plugin's own path alone.
The `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID=` deny (`:64`) runs first and stays: a body naming that assignment is denied in a lane
(fixture), and the finder and verifier briefs say to write the variable's name without `=` beside it. Known limit,
recorded in `docs/agents.md`.

## Probes first (round 2, changes 4 and 5)

Two person-run probes come before the work that depends on them; the build stops at each with the command to run.

1. **Permission probe — before `commands/hef.review.md` is rewritten.** After `review-repro.sh`, `code-review-check`
   and the `lane-guard.sh` exception exist and their smoke parts are green, a person runs, from a plain shell, one
   headless `claude -p` with the verify permission set (the launcher's `--allowedTools` for verify,
   `--disallowedTools Edit,Write`, `--permission-prompts none`, the worker sandbox settings) asking it to run the
   documented `code-review-check` and `review-repro.sh` heredoc calls with `gh` in the bodies, and
   `speckit-helper.sh review-route` (which reads the ledger from inside the sandbox — `ledger.sh dir`/`show`), and the
   same three calls in a verify lane of a `--lanes` project. The exact command line is written into `tasks.md`. Pass = both ran in both modes. If the
   headless matcher refuses the heredoc, the build stops `blocked` with the transcript line — the channel is
   redesigned before the command depends on it.
2. **Eval probe — before the other 17 replay cases.** `review-replay-probe` (scaffolded like d22-3) asks the model to
   run `git --version`, `review-route`, the command's pre-flight (`branch`, `pr-files`), one `review-repro.sh` recipe,
   and to read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/review-repro.sh`; graders: `tool_used` with `input_match` on each call,
   plus `review-route` printing `exhaustive full spec:…` (the `.git/HEAD` path, since git is denied). `d22-3` runs in
   the same eval to learn whether `tool_used` sees a subagent's Bash calls. The other 17 cases are built only after
   the person records the outcome in `evals/README.md`. **A recipe must have run (amendment A2):** the person records
   `review-repro.sh`'s printed `exit:` line and the helper's exit status in `evals/README.md`; if the helper refused
   there (exit 2) or printed no `exit:` line, the build stops `blocked` before the other 17 cases, as probe 1 does —
   the channel is redesigned for the eval sandbox first. The probe case grades that the `exit: 0` line appears. On the measured fact (git denied, `evals/README.md:27`) the
   design already ships `.git/hef-review.diff`, routes from `.git/HEAD`, and copies without git. Defects whose
   reproduction needs git or host state grade on the finding alone (`REPRODUCED` or `UNREPRODUCED`, blocking):
   **D22-1, D22-4, D22-5, D22-6** (`.git/config` rewrites), **D25-3** (systemd < 253), **D31-2** (a ref through the
   worker's git). If git turns out allowed, those rubrics tighten to `REPRODUCED`; nothing else changes.

## Constitution Compliance
- [x] **Principle 1** (payload not under `.claude/`): every file is at the repository root.
- [x] **Principle 2** (namespaced commands): no new command; two subcommands of the existing helper and one helper.
- [x] **Principle 3** (mutation-tested, tool-call assertions): each check rule, each route branch, the repro guard
  and the lane-guard exception have fixtures and mutations; eval cases grade `tool_used Agent min 6` and a
  `review-repro.sh` call, not only the reply; the reply's limits are recorded.
- [x] **Principle 4** (zero-install): bash, `grep`, `find`, `cp`, `jq` (already required); no `awk`; `timeout` only
  when present; git optional in `review-repro.sh`; evals via the installed `claude` CLI.
- [x] **Principle 5** (helpers fail loudly): `code-review-check` exits 1 with `INCOMPLETE` (never a pass) and 2 on
  empty; `review-route` exits 1 on no branch, a detached HEAD or an unreadable entry — never `single` at exit 0 when it
  could not look; `review-repro.sh` exits 2/3 naming the cause.

## Risks & Mitigations
| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|--------|------------|
| Six agents per round cost more than one | spend per verify run up | only `light`/`full` items (D11); cost recorded per replay round (FR-018) |
| Finders flood with weak candidates | verifier load, long report | ≤ 8 per verifier; SUGGESTIONs never block; class-refutation by the verifier |
| `UNREPRODUCED` blocks (owner's decision 3) | real-but-unprovable findings fail rounds | `review-repro.sh` makes most recipes runnable; a contested one goes through HEF-57's dispute to the person |
| `review-repro.sh` lets a verify worker execute any recipe | a prompt-injected recipe from the diff runs | inside the OS sandbox (network allow list, limited writes), on a scratch copy with its own repository; worktree changes fail loudly; same class as running the branch's tests today; dedicated security tests (19s) |
| The heredoc call is refused by the headless permission matcher | every exhaustive round `INCOMPLETE` | permission probe 1 runs before the command depends on it |
| The `lane-guard.sh` exception is too wide | a lane runs an excluded command outside the sandbox | head must be exactly one of two non-excluded helper paths; near-miss fixtures mutation-tested |
| Model writes a report the check rejects for format | spurious INCOMPLETE → FAIL | the verdict is computed, not written; one `[shape]`-only re-format retry |
| Replay fixtures miss host state, or git is denied | a case cannot reproduce | six cases grade on the finding alone; eval probe 2 records the sandbox's limits first |
| The answer key is readable in the with arm | an optimistic replay | recorded as a known limit; a run that reads it is discarded |
| `BLOCKING` line over 500 chars | builder misses a blocker | `… +k more`; ≤ 8-word defects keep ~10 blockers; recipes capped in the shared summary, the rest in the transcript |

## Quick Start
1. `hooks/code-review-lib.sh`, `hooks/review-repro.sh`, the dispatch, the `lane-guard.sh` exception, and smoke parts
   19/19s (red first).
2. Permission probe 1 (person) — stop until it passes.
3. Rewrite `agents/code-reviewer.md` and `commands/hef.review.md` code mode.
4. The shared scaffold, `review-replay-probe` and d22-3; eval probe 2 (person) — then the other 17 replay cases and
   the 3 controls.
5. Docs, README, architecture count, CHANGELOG, evals README; full `tests/smoke.sh` + `node --test`.
